name: AI-powered webpage audit tool listed on Acquire.com (https://app.acquire.com/startup/tlreg50jiy-ai-powered-audit-tool-that-enhances-ux-and-boosts-conversion-offering-white-label-cro-audits)
demand: The closest public search-intent proxy I found is 2,400 average monthly US searches for “website audit tool,” updated 12 July 2026; the provider says its data comes from Google Ads API, but it is not AI- or CRO-specific and UK volume is unverified (https://www.seodata.dev/keyword/website-audit-tool). As market context rather than buyer demand, W3Techs reports WordPress on 39.6% and Shopify on 5.3% of websites in October 2026 (https://w3techs.com/technologies/overview/content_management?wfoid=7822962864.1781136000). ClearAudit claims 129 sites audited in the last 30 days from its own audit history; this is a vendor-reported metric, not independently verified (https://clearaudit.space/). I found no independently verified installs or paid-user count for the Acquire listing.
prices: Public alternatives put pressure on willingness to pay: Webspector offers 3 full reports/month free, then $19/month or $49/month (https://webspector.app/); UX Audit lists an Agency plan at $99/month and a single report at $39 (https://uxaudit.app/pricing); VibeAudit lists $29, $99, and $299 monthly tiers (https://vibeauditapp.com/); Cruelx lists a full report at $8.99 one-time (https://www.cruelx.com/). ClearAudit advertises 2 free audits/month and paid plans from ₹199/month (https://clearaudit.space/). Google’s open-source Lighthouse also audits performance, accessibility, SEO, and other page quality signals, though that is not a full CRO equivalent (https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/overview).

revenue_proof.claim: Acquire’s public listing states an asking price of $20,000, annual revenue of $5,942, and annual profit of $5,942. No underlying transaction records, accounting period, or independently verifiable payment evidence are shown on the public listing; assign zero underwriting weight until dated source records are checked.

copy_speed: High category copyability; these are adjacent launches rather than verified exact clones. PageLens AI says it launched on Product Hunt on 28 April 2026 and describes website/app audits with evidence and fixes (https://www.pagelensai.com/blog). Outbound Autonomy announced its website audit launch on 31 May 2026, covering design, conversion, and technical signals (https://outboundautonomy.com/blog/ph-launch-website-audit-tool). WebAudit AI’s current product offers AI website audits, fixes, verification, monitoring, and white-label reporting; a third-party product record dates its Product Hunt launch to 25 August 2026 (https://webauditaitool.com/; https://inite.ai/en/atlas/webauditaitool.com). The evidence shows rapid adjacent entry, not competitor sales or retention.
platform_risk: Free substitutes cover part of the promise: Lighthouse is open source, and Google PageSpeed Insights provides performance, accessibility, and SEO suggestions (https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/overview; https://developers.google.com/speed/docs/insights/v5/get-started?hl=en). Google’s API documentation says real-world CrUX data in PageSpeed Insights API is planned for discontinuation, illustrating change risk if the product depends on that data; the seller’s actual dependencies are undisclosed (https://developers.google.com/speed/docs/insights/v5/get-started?hl=en). The Acquire listing does not identify the model provider, hosting, crawler, API limits, or transferability of those accounts (https://app.acquire.com/startup/tlreg50jiy-ai-powered-audit-tool-that-enhances-ux-and-boosts-conversion-offering-white-label-cro-audits).
defensible_asset: No defensible asset is evidenced in the public listing: it describes audit features but does not disclose proprietary data, validated rules, integrations, customer switching costs, or transferable contracts (https://app.acquire.com/startup/tlreg50jiy-ai-powered-audit-tool-that-enhances-ux-and-boosts-conversion-offering-white-label-cro-audits). A ruleset and longitudinal benchmark dataset could become assets if verified and legally transferable, but neither is established. Lighthouse is open source, while low-priced competitors already offer AI-generated findings and white-label reports, which limits defensibility from the basic scan/report workflow alone (https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/overview; https://webspector.app/; https://vibeauditapp.com/).
build_effort: Build time for this product is unverified because the listing gives no code, architecture, or scope detail (https://app.acquire.com/startup/tlreg50jiy-ai-powered-audit-tool-that-enhances-ux-and-boosts-conversion-offering-white-label-cro-audits). A solo founder’s dated implementation write-up for an adjacent product describes 40 checks, a crawl of up to 100 pages, one Claude API call for fix instructions, and an estimated $0.03 AI cost per audit; this suggests the core pipeline can be technically compact, but does not verify build time or this seller’s operating cost (https://jethromay.com/articles/i-built-and-launched-auditzap/). Scanning, report generation, billing, and delivery could be automated; support, quality control, and distribution workload are unknown.
channel: Use product-led inbound: publish a useful sample report and search-focused pages, offer a self-serve free audit, and use opt-in founder/product communities or permission-based agency referrals. Do not depend on cold messages. ICO guidance says electronic mail includes social-media direct messages, and sole traders and some partnerships are treated as individual subscribers who generally need consent or a valid soft opt-in for unsolicited marketing; corporate subscribers have different rules (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/; https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guide-to-pecr/electronic-and-telephone-marketing/).
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified. The public listing gives no owner-hours, support volume, or operating procedure (https://app.acquire.com/startup/tlreg50jiy-ai-powered-audit-tool-that-enhances-ux-and-boosts-conversion-offering-white-label-cro-audits).
desk_test: Proposed one-day, no-code test: get seller-provided demo access; make one transparent landing page with a real audit example from a consenting volunteer site and a clearly disclosed refundable beta reservation at $19/month, using Webspector’s public $19/month plan as a price anchor (https://webspector.app/). Share it once in a relevant public opt-in founder community or Product Hunt page, collect inbound reservations, and send no cold DMs or emails. Treat zero paid reservations as a no-go signal, not proof that the whole market is absent. In parallel, request dated payment records and a written owner-hours/support breakdown before assigning value to the listing’s financial claims (https://app.acquire.com/startup/tlreg50jiy-ai-powered-audit-tool-that-enhances-ux-and-boosts-conversion-offering-white-label-cro-audits).
red_flags: This survived the cheap kill-check, but the public evidence does not establish it meets the owner’s hard constraints. The $20,000 ask is about 3.36 times the listing’s claimed $5,942 annual profit, calculated from the listing figures; because the financial period and underlying event date are unverified, that multiple is not reliable underwriting (https://app.acquire.com/startup/tlreg50jiy-ai-powered-audit-tool-that-enhances-ux-and-boosts-conversion-offering-white-label-cro-audits). Agency/white-label growth is a seller-suggested route, not proven demand, and could require sales effort. Weekly owner hours, current automation share, churn, customer concentration, code ownership, and API/model dependencies remain unverified. The numeric 0 in automation_share_pct is an unverified-value sentinel, not a measured 0% automation rate; evidence for >=50% automation and <=5 owner hours/week is absent.
